safety_verdicts.content: Chest pain radiates to the shoulder and neck.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes radiation to left arm/shoulder but does not document radiation to the neck.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS), documenting all radiation patterns (including to the neck/jaw) supports accurate risk characterization and communication to EMS/ED. Omission is unlikely to change immediate management here because other high-risk radiation (left arm/shoulder) and classic pressure symptoms are already documented.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no previous similar episodes of chest pain.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state that there were no prior similar episodes.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether this is a first-ever episode versus recurrent symptoms affects ACS risk stratification and downstream diagnostic framing. Given the patient is already being escalated emergently, the omission is more likely to cause incomplete history rather than a major change in immediate care.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not document haemodynamic stability; instead notes lack of vitals/formal assessment.

In practice ED chest-pain pathways routinely include troponins, so harm is more likely limited to resolution loss rather than a major adverse outcome.
